openQuestions.q: §1.2's forbiddenCatchAlls default set's 8th entry (line 299) is rendered as a code span containing two double-quote characters: `""`. Does this literal mean (a) the 2-character string consisting of two double-quote characters, or (b) the empty string, written in this document's own JSON-value-quoting convention?
openQuestions.evidence: Line 299 raw source: '| `policy.forbiddenCatchAlls` | rejected catch-all patterns (blocklist layer of §1.3) | `.*`, `.+`, `.`, `^$`, `^.*$`, `^.+$`, `\s*`, `""` |' — entries 1-7 are bare, unquoted regex/literal text in code spans (e.g. `.*` = the 2 chars dot-star); by that same convention entry 8's code-span content, read literally, is the 2-char sequence quote-quote, NOT an empty span. This favors the plan's interpretation. HOWEVER lines 74 and 76 of the SAME document establish a different, contradicting convention: 'priorRecordDigest and supersedes carry JSON null (not `""`, not omitted)' and 'Every OTHER optional field is OMITTED entirely when absent — never written as `null` or `""`.' In both of those sentences `""` unambiguously denotes 'the JSON empty string value' (as distinct from null/omission), using JSON-literal quoting to describe a field's possible serialized state. If the table cell at line 299 follows THAT convention instead, entry 8 means the empty string. IMPACT: The frozen policyDigest literal pinned by CHK-003 (independently computed from the spec's exact defaults) depends on which 8th forbiddenCatchAlls entry value is used. The plan resolves this by choosing the 2-character double-quote-literal interpretation, reasoning that an empty-string entry would be logically inert because §1.3 rule 1 already independently requires every matcher value to be non-empty (so an empty string could never reach the forbiddenCatchAlls membership check as a distinguishing rejection reason). That inertness argument is real and does weigh toward the plan's reading, but it is not dispositive — spec authors do sometimes include a logically-redundant belt-and-suspenders default entry for explicitness, and this document's own lines 74/76 convention for this exact notation contradicts the plan's choice. Verdict: NOT independently confirmable from the text alone; genuine ambiguity found on both sides. Recommend the main agent obtain explicit spec-owner clarification (or amend line 299 to spell out 'the empty string' vs the literal `\"\"` unambiguously) before the frozen digest literal is treated as final acceptance evidence.
